title: Incremental typed frames: backpressure and telemetry acceptance
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Context: Customers are integrating LLM outputs with downstream tools and need deterministic, observable incremental output that can be parsed and recovered from under partial failures. This ticket defines acceptance criteria for a new "typed frames" streaming contract (lightweight typed envelope per chunk), a minimal backpressure signal to downstream callers, and required telemetry and dashboards so SRE/SEs can troubleshoot partial outputs and tool-call handoffs. The goal is to enable robust partial consumption, deterministic retries, and clear metrics without changing existing top-level structured-output API surface.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming contract supports typed frames with the following canonical types: INIT, META, FRAME, CHECKPOINT, TOOL_CALL, TOOL_RESULT, ERROR, COMMIT. Each frame is a newline-delimited JSON object with a `frame_type` string and `frame_id` guid.
INIT frame must be emitted at stream start and include `schema_version`, `request_id`, and optional `negotiation` block when schema negotiation is required.
FRAME frames carry partial typed payloads and MUST include `cursor` (byte offset) and `deterministic_seed` when model output must be replayed for idempotent tool calls.
CHECKPOINT frames are durable checkpoints consumers can use to resume; runtime must persist checkpoints for at least 30s and expose `checkpoint_id` in metrics.

TOOL_CALL frames trigger an out-of-band invocation in the tool gateway; they must include `tool_name`, `args_hash`, and `idempotency_token`. The runtime must guarantee at-most-once delivery when idempotency_token is present.
On TOOL_CALL failure (downstream error or timeouts) runtime emits TOOL_CALL with status=failed and then an ERROR frame with normalized `error_code` and `fallback_action` (none|retry|proxy-sync).

Backpressure signal: server may emit a `META` frame containing `backpressure:true` plus `bp_token` and `suggested_rps`. SDKs must surface backpressure to the application and switch to adaptive batching when present.

Partial-output recovery: if a client reconnects with `resume_checkpoint_id`, runtime must resume from the next FRAME after that checkpoint. Tests must include reconnect after a mid-stream TOOL_CALL and verify no duplicate side effects when idempotency_token unchanged.

Telemetry: emit metrics with these names and tags: streaming.frames.count, streaming.frames.by_type, tool_call.latency_ms, tool_call.attempts, streaming.backpressure.events, stream.resume.success. All metrics must include `project`, `model`, `request_id`, and `tenant` tags.

Logs: for every TOOL_CALL emit trace-level event linking request_id->frame_id->tool_call_id and persistent span for 7 days. Console must surface recent failed handoffs and top 5 active backpressure-generating requests.
Compatibility: existing non-framed streaming clients must continue to receive full-text stream as before (compatibility mode). Framed mode is opt-in via header `X-Redwood-Frames:1`.

Security: frames must not leak secrets; TOOL_CALL frames with sensitive args require runtime option `secure_tool_invocation=true` which enforces KMS-wrapped arg blobs and audit-log entries for args access.
Docs: acceptance requires a concise spec doc (PRD + API appendix) and three example SDK snippets (Node, Python, Java) showing resume, backpressure handling, and tool-call idempotency.
Performance: enabling framed streaming must not increase median token latency by more than 6% in the hosted API perf profile for 8k context workloads (measured on runtime-1.22 nightly test harness).
out_of_scope: Heavy-weight schema negotiation protocol (full protobuf/choreo); only small JSON negotiation block supported
Changing underlying model tokenization or model-level caching behavior
Automatic tool-call semantic retries beyond idempotency-token-at-most-once guarantees (complex orchestration will be handled by a later feature)
notes: Design trade-offs: typed frames make failure boundaries explicit but add small per-frame overhead — we limit checkpoint frequency to balance cost vs. resumability.
We prefer idempotency_token as the canonical dedupe primitive instead of deducing from args_hash to avoid accidental collisions across tool versions.
SDK surface: expose a `ResumeController` with `onBackpressure` callback and `withIdempotency(token)` helper for tool calls.
Link to prototype experiment: docs/prototypes/typed-frames-experiment-2026.md (internal drive) and PR on runtime: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/7892
risks: Misuse of backpressure by clients leading to throttling loops — mitigation: grace counters and server-side adaptive cooldowns
Increased operational complexity for tool gateway owners to guarantee at-most-once semantics across retries
Users failing to adopt idempotency tokens causing duplicate side-effects.
qa_plan: Unit tests for frame parsing and validation (positive and negative cases)
End-to-end tests: simulated intermittent network with resume from checkpoint and assertion that downstream tool received single call when idempotency_token present
Load test: enable frames for 1% of production traffic for 48h and validate metric SLAs
Security review: review secure_tool_invocation path for argument exposure in logs
release_plan: Phase 1: opt-in framed streaming behind header `X-Redwood-Frames:1` (canary at 1% hosts)
Phase 2: enable telemetry dashboards and alerting (slo: stream.resume.success > 99.5%)
Phase 3: documentation & SDK rollout, migrate example customers by invite
Rollback: header toggled off and resume points invalidated; ensure console shows affected requests
